title: Legends of Saints & Sinners. Collected and Translated from the Irish

The tales aim to present a narrative that has been shaped by Christian themes while retaining elements of ancient Irish beliefs. Following the introduction, the first legend, "St. Patrick and Crom Dubh," recounts the dark and violent legend of Crom Dubh, an evil chieftain whose oppressive rule is challenged by St. Patrick. This tale sets the tone for the collection, combining themes of good versus evil while establishing the complexities of Irish identity through mythological narratives.
